subject.title: Decouple mode="session" from thread binding requirement

question: Should `sessions_spawn` support persistent `mode="session"` without channel thread binding, and what delivery/lifecycle semantics should unbound native and ACP child sessions use?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the desired behavior affects product-level routing, parent orchestration, cleanup, and channel ownership boundaries that the current code intentionally couples to thread binding.

options.title: Design unbound persistent sessions
options.body: Specify parent-owned unbound session semantics and implement native/ACP parity with focused routing, lifecycle, and non-thread channel proof.

options.title: Keep sessions thread-bound
options.body: Retain the current contract and close or retitle related requests after documenting that persistent interactive sessions require a bindable conversation or thread.

options.title: Split ACP affinity first
options.body: Handle ACP-only cron/orchestrator affinity in a narrower design while leaving native subagent session mode thread-bound for now.

recommendation.title: Design unbound persistent sessions
recommendation.body: Specify parent-owned unbound session semantics and implement native/ACP parity with focused routing, lifecycle, and non-thread channel proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged thread-bound subagent and ACP session work that set the current contract.
